extracted.intended_audience: general readers and students of 19th-century historical biography / readers of Thomas Carlyle
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and evaluative observations drawn from a 19th-century historical-biographical chapter on Friedrich II: guidance on source selection, accounts of upbringing, characterizing influences, and measures of effective governance and administration. Useful for authors or critics assessing biographies, upbringing narratives, or political leadership in historical prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pedantic, 'dryasdust' histories
rubrics_metrics.description: Books that handle Friedrich's childhood are 'mainly of the sad sort' done by 'pedants and tenebrific persons' who 'dwell not on things, but, at endless length, on the outer husks of things' and tend to 'fill the mind with mere dust-whirlwinds.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: overly pedantic, excessively detailed accounts that obscure human actuality. Preference: narratives that focus on lived facts and human insight rather than interminable, confusing minutiae. If compiling or judging biography, penalize accounts that are mere 'outer husks' or lack an index and human interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value first-hand human memoirs despite bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Wilhelmina's memoirs are characterized as 'a human Book ... full of mistakes ... and exaggerates dreadfully ... but is above intending to deceive' and called a 'VERACIOUS Book' of deeper veracity than superficial sorts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat eyewitness or intimate memoirs as valuable sources of human truth; however, explicitly account for their bias: Carlyle suggests deducting 'perhaps twenty-five per cent, or in extreme cases as high as seventy-five' from such accounts to compensate for exaggeration. In evaluation, weigh sincerity and insight more highly than mechanical completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and articulate distinct formative elements (e.g., French vs German)
rubrics_metrics.description: Friedrich's upbringing has 'two elements noticeable, widely diverse: the French and the German. This is perhaps the chief peculiarity; best worth laying hold of.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing a subject's early formation, separate and describe the discrete cultural/educational influences rather than treating upbringing as monolithic. Explicitly show how contrasting elements (language, manners, values) contribute to character.

rubrics_metrics.name: French educational virtues: honor, clearness, truth of word, decorous bearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The French (Edict-of-Nantes) element 'at lowest, there are no conscious semi-falsities, or volunteer hypocrisies ... honor, clearness, truth of word at least; a decorous dignified bearing; various thin good things, are honestly inculcated and exemplified.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing a moral or pedagogical influence, look for inculcation of sincerity, clear manners, and decorum. Note limits: Carlyle calls it 'clear and pure' but 'somewhat barren and meagre' — record both strengths and deficiencies of such cultural schooling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governess/guardian qualities: vigilance, honesty, practical care
rubrics_metrics.description: Dame de Roucoulles 'did her function very honestly' supervising nurses, diet, early physical and intellectual development; she had to be 'very vigilant' over the boy's occasional ill-health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate caretaking figures by practical competence (health, manners, basic instruction), honesty of performance, and attentiveness. Exemplars are credited for faithful, non-theatrical stewardship rather than grandiose pedagogy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language shapes thought (learned to 'think' in a language)
rubrics_metrics.description: From French nurses and governesses, Friedrich 'learned to speak, and likewise, what is more important; to THINK, in French; which was otherwise quite domesticated in the Palace, and became his second mother-tongue.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In biography and cultural analysis, treat language acquisition not merely as communication skill but as formative of thought and perspective. Record the deep cognitive influence of a secondary language on worldview and expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: German/martial educational virtues: ruggedness, practicality, inventiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The native German element is represented by 'born Hyperboreans ... rough as hemp, and stout of fibre' and figures like Prince Leopold who display 'mother-wit', inventiveness (e.g., 'iron ramrod'), 'drilling to perfection', and an appetite for practical military work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging formative influences, capture pragmatic and martial virtues: physical rigor, practical innovations, discipline. Use concrete examples (inventions, drill, campaign experience) as evidence of this strand's impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship under an exacting ruler produces practical wisdom
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'unconscious Apprenticeship' to King Friedrich Wilhelm — 'a harsh Master and almost half-mad ... yet a true and solid one, whose real wisdom was worth that of all the others' — was 'by far the most important element of his education.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the formative effect of powerful, exacting mentors by the practical competencies and mental habits they instill (discipline, economy, solidity) even when their methods are severe. Do not discount hard, austere influence as merely cruelty if it yields demonstrable capacities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance criterion: ruthless economy and elimination of sham
rubrics_metrics.description: Friedrich Wilhelm 'reduced his Household ... to the lowest footing of the indispensable' and 'shears everything down' in expenses. He sought 'perfect economy and solidity, of utility pure and simple' and hated 'wind and blauer dunst' (wind and blue vapor) — i.e., empty show or hypocrisy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate statesmanship and administration by concrete measures of utility: elimination of superfluous posts, strict auditing of pensions and horses, minimal yet effective staffing, and active expunging of corrupt or merely ceremonial waste. Value reality over appearances and penalize 'empty bladders' of formality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure of leadership sincerity: active hostility to mendacity and sham
rubrics_metrics.description: The King has 'a divine idea of fact put into him; the genus sham was never hatefuler to any man' and he 'steadily ... compelling every item ... to take that same character of perfect economy and solidity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In evaluating leaders, score highly those who demonstrate an active hatred of sham and hypocrisy manifested through policy and practice (not rhetoric). Look for structural reforms, repeated auditing, and insistence on substance rather than ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source and style judgement: prefer human insight over tombstone exactness
rubrics_metrics.description: Carlyle criticizes 'dull tombstone' biographical style that lacks life; he praises 'human' writing that gives 'a veracity deeper than the superficial sort' even when imperfect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For editorial standards in biography, prioritize lively, insight-rich prose that conveys human character and causation. Penalize accounts that are merely factual lists with no interpretive or humanizing power; when using precise documentary work, supplement it with humane interpretation.
